procedure.description: panniculectomy with excision of excess skin and subcutaneous tissue of the abdomen

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Copperfield Health denied the claim for CPT 15847 (panniculectomy with excision of excess skin and subcutaneous tissue of the abdomen) with date of service 2026-06-23. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: The documentation does not establish a functional impairment or failure of conservative treatment of the skin condition.

criteria.text: Panniculus hangs at or below the level of the pubis (grade 2 or higher) as documented on examination.

Recurrent or chronic intertrigo, cellulitis, or skin breakdown beneath the panniculus that has failed at least 3 months of conservative treatment such as topical antifungals, hygiene measures, and barrier products.
Weight stable within 10 pounds for at least 6 months.
The panniculus interferes with activities of daily living or ambulation.

chart.text: Vitamin D came back 18. Started 1000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.
From the referring physician: please evaluate for surgical management. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.

Knee pain going down stairs, right side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.

43 year old woman here about the abdominal apron after her weight loss. Nice result on the weight. Discussed panniculectomy versus a full abdominoplasty and what insurance will and will not look at. Her history otherwise: hypothyroidism on levothyroxine, reflux on omeprazole as needed. Allergies: sulfa, hives as a child. Quit smoking 15 years ago, no alcohol, retired. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. On exam the pannus hangs well below the pubis, I would call it grade 3, with maceration and an odor in the fold. She has been fighting the rash under the apron for better than a year, treated with nystatin, then clotrimazole, keeps it dry with powder and a cloth liner, and it comes right back. Two rounds of antibiotics from the PCP for cellulitis in the fold. Down 111 pounds after the sleeve in 2023. Weight has been steady at 196 give or take five for the last 14 months. Says she cannot walk more than a block without the skin fold chafing raw, has to lift it to wash underneath, cannot find pants that fit over it.
Patient called about a tick bite on the calf after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.

Follow-up on the abdomen. Went back over the operation, drains, the scar, recovery of four to six weeks. She understands this is skin and fat removal for the skin problems, not a tummy tuck. Vitals today 141 over 73, pulse 72. Rash is back again despite 9 months of the antifungal and barrier routine. Fold is red and weeping today. Weight 194 today, holding.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.

Here with a cough and congestion for 9 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
She called asking where things stand with the insurance. Told her the paperwork went in and we are waiting to hear. Reviewed what to do in the meantime.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
Interval visit. Nothing new since last time, symptoms as described before, she is managing. Went over the plan again and answered questions from her spouse.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 15 and 14. No ocular pathology noted.
Mammogram report forwarded for the record. Bilateral screening, BI-RADS 1, negative, routine screening in one year.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 4 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.

Mole on the right calf that her spouse noticed. About 7 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
A1c came back 6.5. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Blood pressure check. 123 over 76 today, 130 over 87 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 40 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Work note requested for a sick day last Monday. Faxed to the employer.
Pre-op. Consent signed. Marked the resection with her standing. Nicotine negative. Hold the metformin the morning of.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 50 denial can be answered from the record.
